conflicts.meeting_title: Joint City County Committee Meeting June 10, 2025
conflicts.issue: City-County Funding Scope for Durham Museum of History ($500,000 Capital vs. Operating Support)
conflicts.summary: Committee members split over whether the City and County should fulfill the Durham Museum of History's late-stage $500,000 request covering both feasibility planning and operating/staffing expenses.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support fulfilling the $500,000 joint request ahead of final budget adoption, including feasibility planning and living-wage staff support.
side_a_arguments: The amount is minimal relative to City and County budgets and builds directly on prior feasibility investments.
Supporting living-wage increases aligns with local government priorities and advances a signature Belt Line cultural and tourism destination.
conflicts.side_b_position: Restrict local government support to capital/feasibility planning and avoid last-minute budget additions for nonprofit operating expenses.
side_b_arguments: Final budget work sessions had already taken place, making late operating and new staff-position requests procedurally problematic.
Local governments cannot serve as an open checkbook for nonprofit operating costs across Durham's large nonprofit sector without a clear sustainability and fundraising plan.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; committee members directed discussion toward capital/feasibility alignment and sustainability planning outside the committee session (individual speakers were not identified by name in the audio transcript).

conflicts.meeting_title: Joint City County Committee Meeting June 10, 2025
conflicts.issue: Coalition to End the HIV Epidemic Intake System Critique and Standalone Dashboard Request
conflicts.summary: Coalition presenters and committee officials disagreed on whether Durham's centralized DSS/Entry Point homelessness intake fails HIV-positive residents and whether the Coalition should receive $2.5 million for a separate system and dashboard.
conflicts.side_a_position: Replace reliance on centralized DSS/Entry Point intake with a decentralized, Coalition-led 'no wrong door' care system, standalone data dashboard, and $2.5 million in funding.
side_a_arguments: HIV-positive patients referred to DSS frequently fail to receive housing placements, and centralized intake creates privacy and access barriers.
Existing HIV providers lack funding, capacity, and a formal seat at Consolidated Plan and Action Plan tables despite HOPWA funds sitting unspent.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain Continuum of Care coordinated entry standards, integrate any HIV data into the unified homeless strategic plan, and award nonprofit funds only via competitive RFP.
side_b_arguments: Durham already operates a Continuum of Care-required 'no wrong door' coordinated entry system rather than an exclusionary single-door process.
Building a separate dashboard outside the broader homeless strategic plan duplicates effort, and under tight budgets any nonprofit funding must go through an RFP process.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; officials asked staff to ensure HIV housing needs are coordinated within the broader homelessness strategic plan and RFP framework (individual speakers were not identified by name in the audio transcript).

meetings.title: BOCC/City Council/BOE Join Meeting for Tuesday, August 12, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners, City Council, and Board of Education held a joint meeting on August 12, 2025. The bodies discussed youth funding and programs across county and municipal levels, Durham Public Schools after-school and Encore programs, bicycle and pedestrian transportation gap planning, and an update on tropical storm flood recovery coordination following historic flooding from the remnants of Tropical Storm Chantal.

agenda_items.title: Overview of Youth-Related Funding in Durham County Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County budget staff presented an overview of broad youth-related spending for the current fiscal year, noting that approximately $276 million (about 40% of the general fund budget) goes toward youth services, with Durham Public Schools receiving the lion's share at $224 million. Officials discussed the breakdown of these funds across health, social services, and strategic partnerships, as well as approximately $61 million in debt service for school facilities. Elected officials from the county, city, and school board discussed the scaling of programs, challenges around the expiration of ARPA funds, and the need for ongoing youth programming and transportation support.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Community Education After-School Programs & Partnerships Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Danner and Tracy Super Edwards presented an overview of DPS community education after-school and before-school programs, middle school Encore programs, enrollment trends, and waitlists. They highlighted a new non-state licensing pilot across eight schools to address staffing recruitment barriers and background check hurdles, as well as a new partnership with the Boys and Girls Club of Durham. Board members and council members discussed enrollment demographics, tuition, financial assistance, and the need for accessible after-school activities for middle-school-aged youth.

agenda_items.title: Joint Bike-Walk Plan and Transportation Infrastructure Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and elected officials discussed regional bike-walk plans, project prioritization, gaps in pedestrian infrastructure, and specific school access points such as Northern High School and Marie Massenberg Elementary. Board members inquired about family responsibility zones, bus schedules, crossing guard staffing pilots, and pedestrian connections to school properties. Staff clarified easement arrangements and upcoming public engagement opportunities for transit gap projects.

agenda_items.title: Tropical Storm Recovery Coordination and Emergency Management Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Chief of Emergency Management Nathan Sanders provided an update on response and recovery efforts following Tropical Storm Chantal (July 4-7, 2025), which resulted in historical flooding on the Eno River (reaching 25.63 feet, surpassing Hurricane Fran levels). The presentation covered 81 water rescues by the fire department, emergency non-congregate housing support, coordination with state/federal agencies, the opening of the Disaster Recovery Center at North Regional Library, and individual assistance categories. Elected officials praised first responders, discussed Eno flood gauge monitoring, future infrastructure resilience, and the joint city-county crisis communications plan.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments and Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board checked for public comment sign-ups, confirmed none were present, and discussed future meeting scheduling logistics between the county commissioners, city council, and school board, including aligning meeting cadence with the budget cycle and interlocal agreement streamlining. The meeting was then formally adjourned upon motion and second.

meetings.title: Joint City County Committee Meeting June 10, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Committee met with Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton representing City leadership while Mayor Leonardo Williams was traveling. Staff from Durham County Justice Services, the City Community Safety Department (HEART), Housing for New Homes, and Duke University presented cross-system data and pilot results from the Familiar Faces / Familiar Neighbors initiative, alongside plans to launch a homelessness strategic plan with Community Solutions in July 2025. The Coalition to End the HIV Epidemic in Durham proposed a $2.5 million three-year coordinated care and housing system and criticized DSS/Entry Point bottlenecks, prompting pushback from elected officials over existing Continuum of Care workflows, dashboard integration, and competitive RFP requirements. Committee members also reviewed a $500,000 joint funding request from the Durham Museum of History—debating whether local governments should fund nonprofit operating costs—and discussed coordinating fragmented before- and after-school childcare with Durham Public Schools; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome, and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee leaders opened the Joint City-County Committee meeting at City Hall and noted that Mayor Leonardo Williams was traveling on behalf of the City while Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton was present. Elected officials from the City Council and Board of County Commissioners welcomed students, families, and Durham Public Schools staff before beginning the presentations.

agenda_items.title: Familiar Faces / Familiar Neighbors Initiative and Homelessness Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Justice Services Director, City Community Safety Director Ryan Smith, Housing for New Homes Executive Director Russell Pierce, Duke researcher Nicole, and Community Safety strategist Sheila presented merged detention, Duke Health ED, Alliance Health, and HEART crisis-response data showing that 76 residents accounted for roughly 15% of all 2024 arrests (12 to 36 arrests each) and that co-occurring serious mental illness, substance use disorder, and chronic homelessness drive repeated system cycling. Staff detailed intensive field outreach under the joint pilot—including cases taking over 400 days to secure IDs, SSI income, and permanent supportive housing—and highlighted gaps in non-congregate shelter, street psychiatry, and real-time data sharing. Officials also received an update on a City Manager-directed homelessness system strategic plan launching in July 2025 with Community Solutions (Built for Zero) to produce a governance framework by December 2025.

agenda_items.title: Coalition to End the HIV Epidemic in Durham — Housing and Care System Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Haley Cunningham and Yolanda Foster (Southeast Community Resources) presented on behalf of the Coalition to End the HIV Epidemic in Durham, emphasizing that Black and Latino residents comprise 74% of local HIV cases and that unstable housing sharply elevates AIDS mortality and blocks viral suppression. Presenters criticized fragmented City/County systems and centralized DSS/Entry Point bottlenecks, requesting $2.5 million over three years for a community-led 'no wrong door' care system, an integrated data dashboard, and inclusion in Five-Year Consolidated and Annual Action Plan planning. Committee members pushed back, stating Durham already operates a Continuum of Care 'no wrong door' coordinated entry system, insisting dashboards be integrated into the broader homeless strategy rather than siloed, and noting nonprofit funding requires a competitive RFP process.

agenda_items.title: Durham Museum of History Belt Line Facility and Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum of History representatives outlined plans for a signature cultural destination along the Durham Belt Line / Rail Trail and requested $500,000 jointly from the City and County for feasibility planning and operating/living-wage staffing support (including an education coordinator). While some members expressed enthusiasm for the Belt Line trail-side museum vision and capital feasibility study, other committee members raised concerns that budget work sessions had already concluded and argued that local governments should limit funding to capital projects rather than underwriting recurring nonprofit operating expenses without a sustainability plan.

agenda_items.title: Before- and After-School Care Coordination and Joint City-County-DPS Work Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee members discussed fragmented before- and after-school childcare across Durham Parks and Recreation, DPS Community Education waitlists, and nonprofit providers such as the Boys & Girls Club and Early Years/Durham PreK, recommending a focused presentation at the August joint meeting with DPS. Members also revisited a September 2024 DPS request for a three-entity (City, County, DPS) working group and urged staff to develop a more strategic, proactive multi-body work plan covering childcare, transit, school walk zones, land-use infrastructure, and economic development to avoid program duplication and reduce recurring tax increases.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City-County Committee Meeting 02.11.25
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Committee held an informational work session focused on youth engagement, Durham Public Schools (DPS) student transportation, and county-city youth violence intervention programs. Office on Youth staff discussed scaling paid youth leadership beyond 18 grantees and a 480-practitioner listserv, while elected officials urged better outreach to school teachers and explored future downtown youth center space. DPS Superintendent Dr. Lewis and transportation planners reported adding 15 bus drivers since January 6 to restore full route coverage by January 23, outlined Family Responsibility Zones across 21 elementary schools and Safe Routes to School transit initiatives, and fielded committee questions urging an immediate City-County-DPS staff working meeting on walk-zone hazards. Finally, Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS) Director briefed members on Project Build (95 active youth) and My Brother's Keeper Durham, including plans to hire a youth data analyst and expand Project Build to ages 10–13; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Office on Youth and Youth Leadership Engagement Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office on Youth staff answered committee questions on scaling partnerships across 18 grantees and a 480-plus practitioner listserv, highlighting paid youth consultant roles that have engaged over 300 young people in participatory budgeting and the Comprehensive Plan. Officials discussed aligning community youth data reports with DPS attendance and graduation metrics, expanding direct outreach to middle and high school teachers, reaching disconnected youth via Project Build and My Brother's Keeper, and potentially utilizing existing downtown space such as a relocated Convention Center for a youth center.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Transportation, Family Responsibility Zones, and Safe Routes to School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Superintendent Dr. Lewis, interim Auxiliary Services Executive Director Ken Barnes, and DPS school planning staff reported hiring 15 new bus drivers since January 6 and restoring route coverage across all schools as of January 23, while implementing Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) within a one-mile radius at 21 of 32 elementary schools. Presenters detailed driver retention proposals, GoDurham secondary-school transit guides, Safe Routes to School safety grants, and requests for City/County bus shelters, traffic calming, and piloted contracted crossing guards. Committee members urged state-level advocacy for bus driver pay, questioned safety and equity impacts of elementary walk zones, asked about hiring justice-involved residents, and pressed City, County, and DPS staff to convene immediately on walk-zone infrastructure fixes.

agenda_items.title: Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS): Project Build and My Brother's Keeper
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CISS Director presented operational updates on Project Build—serving 95 active youth ages 14 to 21 under the Comprehensive Gang Model with joint City, County, and JCPC funding—and My Brother's Keeper Durham, including a 80-plus student summit, podcast, and Divine Nine mentoring partnerships. CISS outlined plans to establish a countywide youth-services data hub via a newly hired analyst, expand Project Build to ages 10 to 13 in the upcoming budget cycle, and collaborate with City Community Safety Director Ryan Smith on a comprehensive community safety plan. Committee members praised Project Build's outcomes and urged staff to coordinate with prior youth safety assessments to avoid duplicating efforts.
